clue.text: Front man whole number precede

parts.note: a figure is a numeral, a whole number
to head something is to go before it

explanation.surface: An odd instruction about a leading man and putting a number first.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurehead is a nominal leader with no real power, someone who fronts an organisation.

clue.text: Female provided with English flute

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
'provided' as a conjunction means if
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A woman is handed an English flute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provided with' reads as one phrase, but 'provided' is the conjunction meaning if, and 'with' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A fife is a small high-pitched flute played in military bands.

clue.text: Origin of Danger Mouse

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the following words, forming part of them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: The backstory of Danger Mouse, a British cartoon secret-agent mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Danger Mouse was a British children's cartoon about a mouse spy, which makes the clue read like a question about the character's beginnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is the seed or starting point from which something develops, so it is an origin.

clue.text: Berkshire university — good girls may wear these during tutorials

parts.note: the University of Reading is in the county town of Berkshire
G is the abbreviation for good
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Female students at Reading University wear something for their tutorials.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town in Berkshire, an English county west of London, with its own university; the 'good girls' sound like diligent students.
explanation.definitionFit: Students studying in tutorials might put on spectacles meant for close work on the page.

clue.text: Rodent in middle of the stream, swimming

indicators.note: only the central letter of the following short word is kept

parts.note: the centre letter of this three-letter word

indicators.note: something swimming moves about, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A small animal is found paddling in the middle of a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of the stream' looks like one phrase, but 'middle of' acts only on 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small burrowing rodent, often kept as a pet.

clue.text: Has an ambitious plan when shown round tower

indicators.note: one piece is placed around another, enclosing it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
a spire is a tall pointed tower on a church

explanation.surface: Someone with grand designs is given a tour around a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to have a strong ambition to achieve something.

clue.text: Ornamental case used in piqué tuition

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the following words, contained in them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A decorated case features in lessons on piqué, a ribbed fabric or inlay work.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent on piqué is ignored, as crosswords ignore accents.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small decorative case for needles, cosmetics or other small articles.

clue.text: Artist's subject, unhappy little chappie

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Gainsborough's famous portrait of a boy in a blue satin costume
second meaning, read literally: a sad small lad

explanation.walkthrough: The painting is by Thomas Gainsborough; read word by word, the title also describes a downcast lad, since blue means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: The painting's title names its sitter, and taken literally it means a sad young boy.

clue.text: Secret involving one dead cow

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or include, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: intimate can mean private or personal, kept secret
the Roman numeral for one
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A hidden matter concerning a dead farm animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning to frighten into submission.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to subdue them by threats, which is exactly what intimidating means.

clue.text: Dodgy business practice that began in ancient Egypt?

definitions.text: Dodgy business practice that began in ancient Egypt?

parts.note: surface reading: a fraudulent commercial scheme
setter's reading: the scam is named after the tapering stone monuments of the pharaohs, as if it started there

explanation.walkthrough: The fraud is named for the shape of its recruitment chain, which widens downward like the Egyptian monuments; the question mark flags the joke that it began there.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a scheme where profits depend on recruiting ever more sellers rather than real sales, widely seen as dishonest.

clue.text: Get rid of member bringing gun

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A club expels one of its members for bringing a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is any portable gun, such as a rifle or pistol.

clue.text: Punishment — type man dished out

indicators.note: dishing something out spreads it around, scattering the order of the letters

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A certain kind of man hands out penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment can mean retribution, as when wrongdoers receive their just deserts.

clue.text: Fruit, choice by London station

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece is placed next to the other

parts.note: Victoria is a major London railway terminus
a plum job is a choice, highly desirable one

explanation.surface: Choosing some fruit from a stall next to a London railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: The station comes first in the answer though it is last in the clue, since 'by' allows either order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria is a popular English variety of plum with red-and-yellow skin.

clue.text: Expert on houses?

parts.note: surface reading: a surveyor or estate agent who knows about buildings
setter's reading: the twelve divisions of the sky used in casting horoscopes

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that 'houses' is not property but the twelve zodiac sectors of a horoscope chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A horoscope reader divides the heavens into twelve houses and interprets planets within each.

clue.text: Crooked undertakings causing one to argue

parts.note: bandy legs are bowed or crooked
giving one's word is making a promise or undertaking

explanation.surface: Dishonest promises lead someone to quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' suggests dishonesty, but here it means bent, as in bow legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange words is to have a verbal dispute, so the phrase is an idiom for quarrelling.

clue.text: Endless disease in horses makes one reel

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: the staggers is a disease of horses and cattle causing unsteady gait

explanation.surface: A horse illness causes unsteady swaying.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to sway or totter unsteadily, which is what one does when walking drunkenly or dizzily.

clue.text: A salary and gratuity aboard ship

indicators.note: being aboard means being inside a vessel, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to ship goods is to send them
a tip is a gratuity

explanation.surface: A sailor's wages plus tips earned on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship' looks like a noun for the vessel, but it is the verb meaning dispatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular payment, especially one paid to a clergyman or student.

clue.text: Hold-up, unfortunately, behind start of race for reindeer

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other, following it
only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so the letters end up in a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A delay at the start of a reindeer race.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph is the red-nosed reindeer of the Christmas song who leads Santa's sleigh.

clue.text: Number, following try, cheer

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A rugby number scores a try and the crowd cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' suggests rugby, but here it means to judge a case in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to encourage or lift their spirits.

clue.text: Complete one's training in shop as souter

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An apprentice cobbler finishes training in the shop; a souter is a Scots word for shoemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Recruits and cadets pass out when they finish training and graduate, often with a parade.

clue.text: This'll support climbers galore, scrambling under pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry, going under puts one piece below the other

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: scrambling mixes things up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mountaineers scrambling up under pressure need something to grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbers' suggests mountaineers, but means climbing plants such as roses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is a garden framework of posts and beams over which climbing plants are trained.

clue.text: Children's author's wife brought in fresh éclairs and burger bun

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside
fresh means new, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, ignoring the accent
W is the abbreviation for wife
a bread roll holds a burger

explanation.surface: A writer's wife comes home with pastries and a burger bun.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'author' stands for 'has': the author has the wife inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, a classic for young readers.

clue.text: Pretty fine tune

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A rather good melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty fine' reads as 'quite good', but 'Pretty' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair is an old word for beautiful or attractive, as in 'fair maiden'.

clue.text: Impulsive dramatist? Sounds like it

indicators.note: the answer is pronounced the same as the name of the writer just mentioned

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright of The Importance of Being Earnest

explanation.surface: Asking whether a rash playwright lives up to his reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild behaviour is unrestrained and reckless, acting on impulse.

clue.text: Item of clothing found in untidy manger by second of stalls

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other
something untidy is in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: only the letter in second position of the following word is used

parts.note: the second letter of the word

explanation.surface: Some clothing turns up in a messy feeding trough in the stable stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is any single piece of clothing.

clue.text: Beginning, briefly, to frame American and Japanese art

indicators.note: a frame goes around a picture, so one piece surrounds another
made brief, so the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an origin is a beginning
AM is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American and Japanese art first framed in short order.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese craft of folding paper into decorative shapes.

clue.text: Reckless prang, not chauffeur's first

indicators.note: not having something means it is taken away

parts.note: prang is British slang for a minor car accident

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A careless car smash that wasn't the driver's first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash act is hasty and done without thinking of the consequences.

clue.text: Put in jeopardy as grenade exploded next to border

indicators.note: one piece sits beside the other

parts.note: an end is a boundary or edge

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart, so its letters are scattered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grenade going off near a frontier puts lives at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to expose it to danger or risk of harm.
